messages:
Maria L.: hey infra — trying to bring up a new GKE cluster in asia-southeast1 for batch-gen. plan: node pool of n1-standard-16 with 4x A100 (a100-80gb) per VM, target 3 nodes. hitting quota/alias-ip errors when scaling past 1 node. anyone run into this with GKE alias ranges + GPUs?
Andrew K.: can you paste the error you see from the node bootstrap / kubelet?
Maria L.: paste from controller-manager log:
```
I0318 15:02:41.123456 1 gce_cloud_provider.go:245] Failed to allocate alias IP ranges for node: "projects/our-project/..." : insufficient secondary IP addresses in subnet "subnet-prod-ase1" for the requested reservation
error: failed to create node: PodCIDR allocation failed
```
Maria L.: Also noticed compute.googleapis.com/GPUS quota for region is 4 A100, we need 12 total. I already tried increasing node pool replicas and it fails during instance create.
Samir P.: two separate limits here: (1) regional GPU quota (A100) and (2) secondary IP capacity on the subnet's secondary range used by GKE for Pods. GKE will run out of pod IPs if your secondary range is small or max-pods-per-node is high.
Samir P.: checks we have subnet secondary-range size / allocation? what's the CIDR for the pod range on that subnet?
Maria L.: the pod secondary range is 10.10.16.0/22 (about ~1020 addresses). with our current cluster-autoscaler target and default maxPodsPerNode=110, a 3-node pool x 110 > available addresses after other clusters.
Priya S.: two options: reduce maxPodsPerNode on GPU nodepool (set --max-pods-per-node=32) or expand secondary range (preferred if we want high pod density). reducing max-pods will increase VM count and cost.
Maria L.: cloud-ops, can we request quota bump for A100 regional GPU and ask network team to enlarge the secondary range for subnet-prod-ase1? Also want estimate on time/cost impact if we do smaller max-pods vs expand range.
cloud-ops: opened support case with GCP: CASE-2026-3342. Requested: compute region quota A100 from 4 -> 16 in asia-southeast1, and subnet secondary IP range expansion from /22 -> /20 for pod range. GCP ETA ~48-72h (might be faster).
cloud-ops: For immediate unblock, we can also create a temporary node pool using 2xA100 per VM and only 2 replicas (fits current GPU quota) and set max-pods-per-node=32 to keep pod IP usage lower.
Andrew K.: can we also try using smaller GPU instances (e.g., a100-40gb or v100 if available) to stay within quota while we wait? Might be less throughput but quicker rollout.
Priya S.: cost note: 3x A100-80gb in ase1 ~ estimated $X/hr (including preemptible vs on-demand differences). If we split into more smaller nodes cost goes up ~15% for same GPU count because of overhead. I'll DM cost sheet.
infra-bot: [quota-bot] Ticket CASE-2026-3342 created by cloud-ops. Slack thread updated. :white_check_mark:
Maria L.: thanks all — going to: (1) spin up temp 2-node pool with 2xA100 each + max-pods-per-node=32, (2) keep case open for quota and subnet expansion, (3) flag product for potential slow rollout. will post updates here. :thumbsup:
Samir P.: if you want the gcloud commands, run:
```
gcloud compute addresses update SUBNET_NAME --region=asia-southeast1 --add-secondary-range=pods=10.10.0.0/20
# or request via VPC admin if managed
```
Samir P.: and for nodepool config: `gcloud container node-pools create gpu-pool --cluster=my-cluster --machine-type=n1-standard-16 --num-nodes=2 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=2 --max-pods-per-node=32`
Maria L.: perfect. i'll try the temp pool now and report back.
Priya S.: ping me if this goes to billing approval for larger quota — i'll prep the cost impact note.
Maria L.: update: temp pool created and nodes are Ready. pods scheduling ok. leaving case open until GCP confirms quota and subnet change.
cloud-ops: GCP replied, approved GPU quota increase to 16. subnet expansion still pending, follow-up in 6-12h.
Maria L.: awesome, closing loop once subnet updated. thanks everyone!
